<p class="name">Joris Klingen</p>
<p class="role">Economist at CPB Netherlands Bureau for Economic Policy Analysis</p>

::: {.chips}
<span>Transport</span><span>Urban</span><span>Environmental</span><span>Energy</span><span>Road safety</span><span>Cycling</span>

<img src="images/joris.png" class="portrait" alt="Portrait of Joris Klingen">
:::

At CPB, I work on energy policy.
I hold a PhD from [Spatial Economics at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam](https://spatialeconomics.nl/), supervised by Jos van Ommeren and Erik Verhoef.
Before that, I studied Economics and Econometrics at the [Tinbergen Institute](https://www.tinbergen.nl), Spatial, Transport and Environmental Economics at the VU, and Future Planet Studies at the Universiteit van Amsterdam.
In 2019 I was a visiting researcher with Dan Graham at Imperial College London's [Transport Strategy Centre](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/transport-engineering/transport-strategy-centre/).

My research is empirical work in transport and environmental economics, often built on natural experiments in large public datasets.
I have studied how smartphone use affects road safety, how air pollution slows cyclists and changes risk-taking at the chessboard, and how cyclists respond to metro disruptions and new bike lanes.
Much of this work uses trip data from bike-sharing schemes in Paris, London and New York City.
My current projects, all in New York, look at taxi tipping, e-bike choice and protected bike lanes; see [Research](research.qmd).

I'm also a musician and like to develop music software.
I play keys in [Flamingo Hitmix](https://flamingohitmix.com) and drums in [Bovenburen](https://bovenburen.com) (see also [Music](music.qmd)).
